primary_claim: Appropriate system prompts alone can bring a non-safety-tuned reasoning model's toxic-refusal rate within 5% of a safety-tuned counterpart's, while reducing over-refusal by roughly 2-10x, suggesting prompting may complement or even outperform certain safety-training approaches on these benchmarks.

effect.metric: toxic-refusal rate gap vs. safety-tuned model, and over-refusal reduction on OR-Bench
effect.value: system prompts get DeepSeek-R1-Qwen3-8B within 5% of RealSafe-R1-8B's toxic-refusal rate, with ~2x less over-refusal on OR-Bench-hard and ~5-10x less on OR-Bench-80k

contradicts_or_qualifies: SpecEval (Ahmed et al. 2025) found compliance gaps of up to 20% across providers between model behavior and model specifications, motivating this experiment
RealSafe-R1's safety training (inspired by Deliberative Alignment) results in very high over-refusal (98-100% on OR-Bench-hard), suggesting the safety training overshot into over-conservatism
stated_future_work: Replicate with matched distillation targets, or better, exactly control for instruction tuning and safety training separately
Test whether prompting specifically for over-refusal (e.g. positive statements or in-context examples) can reduce over-refusal in safety-tuned models like RealSafe-R1-8B
limitations_stated: Conclusions rest on the assumption that differing distillation targets (Qwen3-8B vs. Llama-3.1-8B) between the two models don't meaningfully affect the evaluation results
n=3 resampled runs with large observed variance on over-refusal metrics meant no formal hypothesis testing was performed

The large capability gap on MMLU-Pro between the two models is largely attributable to a token limit imposed during evaluation causing DeepSeek to run out of tokens, not necessarily a true capability difference
quote: the usage of these system prompt could get us within 5% of RealSafe's toxic-refusal rates, with ~2x less over-refusal on OR-Bench-hard and ~5-10x less over-refusal on OR-Bench-80k.
